summary:
Our project explores the human-made objects left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions. These objects include landers, rovers, scientific instruments, and other equipment that remain on these celestial bodies after completing their missions.

We developed a storytelling-based concept to highlight the history, purpose, and scientific significance of this discarded equipment. By presenting these objects as part of the story of space exploration, we aim to help people understand why they were left behind, what they contributed to science, and what they represent for future missions.

This project addresses the challenge by turning overlooked space artifacts into meaningful stories. It is important because these objects are not simply abandoned equipment; they represent human innovation, scientific achievements, and the lasting impact of our exploration beyond Earth.
details:
ORBIT MAVEN — Project Details

ORBIT MAVEN is an interactive educational storytelling website developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge under the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars."

Our project explores the human-made machines left behind during space exploration missions. For decades, NASA has sent landers, rovers, probes, and scientific equipment to explore other worlds. While some machines continue operating, others have completed their missions and remain behind. Their stories, contributions, and historical significance deserve to be remembered.

How does it work?

ORBIT MAVEN presents these forgotten explorers through an engaging digital experience. Visitors can explore mission profiles, discover information about space exploration through a timeline, and test their knowledge using an interactive six-question quiz. The website uses storytelling to make scientific and historical information more interesting and accessible.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project raises awareness about the equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. It encourages students, educators, and space enthusiasts to learn about the history of space exploration, appreciate the engineering behind these missions, and understand that even machines whose missions have ended remain part of humanity's scientific legacy.

Our intended impact is to transform overlooked space artifacts into meaningful educational stories and inspire curiosity about space exploration.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of ORBIT MAVEN is its storytelling approach. Instead of presenting discarded equipment as forgotten objects, we give these machines a narrative identity. Our concept connects factual space exploration history with engaging storytelling, supported by an interactive timeline and knowledge quiz. The website's space-inspired visual design also creates an immersive experience.

Tools and Development

The project is developed as a web-based experience and hosted through GitHub Pages. Its visual identity uses a dark cosmic theme, glowing planetary elements, orbital designs, and contrasting colors to reflect the atmosphere of space exploration.

Factors Considered

During development, we focused on educational value, accessibility, simplicity, visual engagement, and the importance of presenting historical information responsibly. We also considered how to make the website interesting for visitors who may have little prior knowledge of space exploration.

Ultimately, ORBIT MAVEN is built around one message: the robots we left behind still have stories to tell.
